newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn ministry denies Eurofighter price agreed.
newsitem.headline: Bonn ministry denies Eurofighter price agreed.

text.p: The German Defence Ministry on Thursday denied a press report that it had come to an agreement with Daimler-Benz Aerospace (DASA) on the price of the planned Eurofighter aircraft.

The Berliner Zeitung said in an advance release from Friday's edition that Defence Minister Volker Ruehe and DASA head Manfred Bischoff were ready to sign a deal pricing Germany's order for 180 aircraft at more than 20 billion marks ($12.75 billion).
But a ministry spokesman said no such agreement could be signed until parliament approved budget financing some time in March. He said talks were continuing in a positive fashion.
A DASA spokesman said he did not know of any agreement.

On Sunday the weekly newspaper Welt am Sonntag said the German coalition parties had hammered out in principle a deal which secured financing for the four-nation Eurofighter project to go ahead this year.
The Defence Ministry declined to confirm this but said it was confident an agreement would be reached by the end of March.
The aircraft are to be delivered between 2002 and 2012 or 2015.

Germany's problems with financing have been holding up the signing of a memorandum of understanding with Britain, Spain, and Italy. British Aerospace Plc, state-controlled Alenia of Italy and state-owned Construcciones Aeronauticas SA of Spain are all partners in the consortium together with DASA.
Britain wants to order 232 of the aircraft, Italy is scheduled to take 140 and Spain 87.
